research.title: BaCon: Band-Concentrated Exponential Random Graph Models
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Exponential-family random graph models ERGMs provide a parametric interpretable framework for modeling real graphs including the Web and social networks Fitted ERGMs may suffer from degeneracy matching observed graph statistics in expectation does not guarantee that. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Community detection in complex networks via node similarity, graph representation learning, and hierarchical clustering
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: Community detection is a significant challenge in analysing real graphs, including social, citation, biological, and many other networks. This article proposes three new, general, hierarchical frameworks to deal with this task. The introduced approach supports various. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Context-Aware Multimodal Claim Verification in Spoken Dialogues
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Spoken factual claims often occur within multi-turn conversations, where surrounding dialogue can provide context unavailable from the claim alone. Yet most fact-checking research evaluates isolated text, leaving conversational audio under-studied. We introduce MAD2, a synthetic Multi-turn. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Interpretable Social Network Churn Prediction via Ergodic Markov Chains
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Predicting social network churn before it becomes visible in aggregate metrics remains an open challenge, particularly in enterprise settings where heterogeneous usage patterns, sparse data, and deployment constraints preclude standard supervised approaches. We formalize this problem. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: When Platforms Pay Users to Correct Misinformation: Revenue Incentives and Governance Capacity in Weibo Annotations
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: Crowdsourced misinformation governance systems such as Community Notes and Weibo Annotations depend on sustained corrective labor. How monetary incentives shape participation and subsequent governance outcomes remains poorly understood. We conduct a mixed-methods study of Weibo Annotations. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
